dehydrated_text:
Achilles was a noble person. Have you no mercy?" And then he kills Pry's son, Polites.

Suddenly, Pry, who had just escaped from the slaughter, saw Pyrus' hands racing through the long arcades and deserted hallways, spearing fleeing enemy fighters. A weapon poised for the kill, about to run Polites through as he reached his parents. Polites collapsed, vomiting out his life blood before their eyes. This is very similar to the death of Hector.

Prime, witnessing this, cries out in rage: "If any power on high recoils at such an outrage, let the gods repay you for all your reckless work. Grant you the thanks, the rich reward you've earned. You've made me see my son's death with my own eyes. Defiled a father's sight with a son's lifeblood."

You say you're Achilles' son. You lie. Achilles never treated enemies so. No, he honored them as suppliants right. He blushed to betray his trust. He restored Hector's bloodless corpse for burial and sent him safely home.

With all his might, the old man flung his spear, but it merely grazed Pyrus' brazen shield. Pyrus shouts back: "Well, then down you go. A messenger to my father, Pelia's son. Tell him about my vicious work." He dragged the old man straight to the altar, quaking and slithering through slicks of his son's blood, twisting Pry's hair in his left hand while his right swept forth a sword that buried itself hill-deep in the king's flank.

Such was the fate of Piriam. His death, his slot on earth with Choi blazing before his eyes, her ramparts down. The monarch who once ruled all his glory over Asia's many tribes.

All Roman schoolchildren have to memorize this poetry. And if you are a Roman schoolchild and know that Pry is from your ancestors, you have a deep hatred of the Greeks. The entire purpose of the Iliad is to create such hatred in order to forge a Roman identity. The Greeks were a civilization based on reflection, debate, openness. This modern reenactment of the play, *The Trojan Women*, discusses what happens to the children and women after Troy falls.

When the Greeks watch this play, they see their own darkness and must feel empathy for their enemies. Civilization is about understanding others. The Romans, however, just want to kill. American football today mirrors this Roman culture. It is violent, barbaric.

The Greeks, for fun, organize symposia where people come together to discuss love, poetry, life. They drink watered-down wine and keep talking. Their entire argument is just to have a conversation.
